clue.text: Hide 80% of bust

indicators.note: eighty per cent of a five-letter word keeps four of its letters, so the final one is lost

parts.note: bust means broke, which in British slang is skint

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal most of a sculpted bust, or of a bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: '80% of' drops the last of SKINT's five letters, giving four of them. SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Eagerly anticipating afters, always very inspired rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns around, so the whole assembled string is read backwards

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, shortened to pud from pudding

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly awaiting dessert, with very inspired bread rolls always on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired' (breathed in) puts V inside the word for always, and 'rolls' turns the whole string, PUDEVVER, round. Afters is the British word for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Being revved up is an idiom for being excited and keyed up, like an engine raced before the off.

clue.text: Zhivago's man, missing dad, initially keeps bones

indicators.note: missing means going without, so letters are taken out of the author's name

parts.note: Boris Pasternak wrote the novel Doctor Zhivago, so he is Zhivago's man
dad is pa

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word keeps

explanation.surface: The man Zhivago, lacking his father, keeps a few bones at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes PA and K (the first letter of 'keeps', by 'initially') out of PASTERNAK. 'Zhivago's man' looks like the doctor himself but is the man who wrote him.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone, so it means more than one of these bones.

clue.text: See, then bribe, fruit supplier

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them
to palm someone is to bribe them, as in greasing a palm

explanation.surface: A corrupt deal: meet someone, pay them off, and a fruit seller is secured.
explanation.definitionFit: A date palm is the tree that bears dates, so it supplies that fruit.

clue.text: Up they go in summer, down they come in winter

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a summer game, a skier is a ball hit high into the air
people coming down snowy slopes in the winter season

explanation.surface: A riddle about things that rise in one season and descend in another.
explanation.walkthrough: A skier in cricket is a mis-hit that goes very high, often to be caught; cricket is the English summer sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a towering cricket shot and a person sliding downhill on skis.

clue.text: Pulling strings, Republicans join the jet set

indicators.note: pulling means towing behind, so the party goes in front and the strings trail after it

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
laces are strings, as in shoelaces

explanation.surface: Political string-pulling by Republicans gets them into the glamorous elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling strings' looks like the idiom for using influence; here the party tows the laces behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go places is an idiom for being successful and rising in the world, as the jet set have done.

clue.text: Waiving fine if champion racer orbits earth

indicators.note: to orbit is to circle round, so the racer's name goes around the small piece

parts.note: Ayrton Senna was a Formula One world champion driver

indicators.note: waiving means letting go of, so a letter is dropped from the little word if

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Without a fine, a champion driver circles the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiving fine' leaves I, which 'orbits' puts inside the driver's name. 'earth' looks like the planet being circled; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is a natural earth pigment, a clay coloured by iron oxide used as paint.

clue.text: When Mother's prodded by son and Father appears, see 1 Diagonal

definitions.text: When Mother's prodded by son and Father appears

indicators.note: prodded means poked, as if the other letters stick into either side of mother

parts.note: by is shown with the multiplication sign X, as in three by four
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
mother is ma

explanation.surface: A family scene: a son nudges mum and Father Christmas arrives, as the diagonal message says.
explanation.walkthrough: X for 'by' comes from dimensions such as 3 x 4. The whole clue also describes Christmas morning, when Father Christmas turns up; 'see 1 Diagonal' points to the seasonal greeting hidden on the grid's diagonal.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas visits at the festive season, the short written form of which uses X for Christ.

clue.text: Look round racecourse to follow developments

indicators.note: turned round means read in the opposite direction, applied to the word for look

parts.note: to peek is to look
a track is a racecourse

explanation.surface: Glance around the racecourse to stay up to date with events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like 'around the racecourse'; it turns PEEK back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep track of things is an idiom for staying informed as they change.

clue.text: Narcotic one's cutting up, about to fill order

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so the other letters sit within the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the combined small piece is read backwards
cutting means slicing into, so the numeral goes into the middle of up

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A drug-themed scene: someone slicing up a narcotic, about to fill an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' makes UIP, 'about' turns it to PIU, and 'to fill' sets that inside the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic drug made from the dried latex of poppies.

clue.text: More than one dream destination resembles the Flying Dutchman?

definitions.meaning: never-never land is an imaginary ideal place, and the plural gives several of them
read as ..., it describes a ship that is doomed never ever to reach port

explanation.surface: A comparison between fantasy holiday spots and a legendary ghost ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Dutchman is a legendary phantom ship condemned to sail forever without making harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-never land is Peter Pan's fantasy island, hence any idyllic imaginary place.

clue.text: Islamic college recycled drama with it

indicators.note: recycled means sent round again, so letters from the end of the word come back to its front

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A religious college reuses a play along with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' brings the last two letters of the play round to the front. 'it' as sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrasa is a school or college for Islamic instruction.

clue.text: Red Sea Commander

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: It reads as a naval officer's title for the Red Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Sea' looks like one name, but Red is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a Bordeaux region whose wine is mainly red claret.

clue.text: Second rogue caught in one rapid movement

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the rogue sits within the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
a cad is a rogue

explanation.surface: In a single second, a rogue is caught in one quick move.
explanation.definitionFit: A saccade is a quick jump of the eyes between fixation points.

clue.text: Throw out Conservative stowed in the back of the plane

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here applied to the
stowed in means packed away inside, so the party letter goes within the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane

explanation.surface: A Tory stowaway at the back of an aircraft is to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the back of the plane' looks like one phrase; the back of 'the' gives E, and the plane is JET.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to expel or throw out forcibly.

clue.text: Go to M&S and enter skirmishes here?

definitions.text: Go to M&S and enter skirmishes here?

parts.note: to go is to depart

indicators.note: skirmishes are scuffling fights, which throw these letters into disorder

parts.note: M and S taken as the bare letters from the shop's initials

explanation.surface: Heading to Marks and Spencer for the sales means joining scuffles in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British high-street chain. The whole clue describes such a shop, with crowds jostling during the sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks and Spencer is a large store selling many kinds of goods in separate sections, a place where shoppers jostle.

clue.text: Present drawers?

parts.note: those that draw, that is pull, Santa's sleigh of gifts; not chests of drawers or underwear

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about the drawers in a piece of furniture today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' looks like furniture or underwear, and 'Present' like 'current'; the drawers here haul a sleigh full of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh, laden with Christmas gifts, is pulled by these antlered animals.

clue.text: Recently delivered feeding line on a talk-show?

indicators.note: feeding into means running through, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A newsreader is fed a script line on a chat show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' marks the answer as concealed in 'line on a talk-show'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal describes babies in their first weeks, those newly born.

clue.text: Elbow grease? That's evident!

parts.note: evident means overt
oil is a grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: An exclamation that hard graft is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Visible grease would be overt oil; elbow grease is slang for hard physical effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtoil means excessive labour, the hard graft that elbow grease names.

clue.text: Hearty chap, rather comical — not today's leading light?

parts.note: a card is a funny, eccentric fellow
the leading light of a grid is normally clue 1ac, written like IAC, but this puzzle has no 1 Across

explanation.surface: A jolly comical fellow is said to be past his best as a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Clues are numbered, and 1 Across usually leads; today the first across clue is 9, so '1ac' is not today's leader. The figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac means relating to the heart, so it fits hearty in a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: With element detailed, Curies finally spoke

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, so the final letter of the element goes

parts.note: radium is a chemical element

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Curies

explanation.surface: The Curies, who discovered an element, finally made a speech about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Curies discovered radium, which makes the element misleadingly apt; 'spoke' looks like a past tense verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A radius is a straight line from a circle's centre to its rim, like a wheel's spoke.

clue.text: Ape's grabbed an awning

indicators.note: grabbed means seized and held, so the short word goes inside

parts.note: to ape is to copy; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A monkey has snatched a shop's canvas sunshade.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering of fabric, such as a shelter above a door.

clue.text: Loaded up, sternward through southern strait, then heading off

indicators.note: going through means passing within, so one piece is set inside the other
heading off means losing the head, the first letter of the strait

parts.note: the Solent is the strait off the south coast of England, by the Isle of Wight

indicators.note: sternward means towards the back of a ship, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A laden ship sails back through a channel in the south, then turns off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims SOLENT to OLENT, and 'sternward' turns UP into PU, which goes 'through' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very wealthy, and opulent means rich and luxurious.

clue.text: Newsgroup inductees energetically screening CID out

indicators.note: energetically means vigorously, so the letters are shaken into a new order
screening means filtering, so some letters are sieved from the pool
out means removed, completing the instruction to take letters away

explanation.surface: New recruits keenly vet out the police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of INDUCTEES, with C, I and D removed, are rearranged. CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is the early internet system of discussion groups, made up of newsgroups.

clue.text: Wrongly attended a baddie

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly, so the following words are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone improperly looked after a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' reorders all the letters of ATTENDED A BADDIE; the whole clue also describes an accomplice's crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aided and abetted is to be helped in committing a crime, wrongful assistance to a villain.

clue.text: Opera's eponymous character the driving force in Carmen?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the force goes within the motoring body

parts.note: read as car men, the AA, Britain's Automobile Association whose patrolmen help motorists
in Freud's theory the id is the instinctive driving force of the mind

explanation.surface: A question whether the opera's title heroine is what drives the opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' looks like Bizet's opera; split it as 'car men' for the AA, a British roadside-rescue organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera Aida is named after its heroine, the Ethiopian princess.

clue.text: The old lizard's in love, subservient to daughter

indicators.note: subservient means lower, so in this down clue the other pieces come beneath the daughter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O

explanation.surface: An old reptile is besotted and obeys a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old lizard's' looks possessive; the 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: Dino is informal shorthand for dinosaur, a giant reptile of prehistoric times.

clue.text: Please exercise duck

parts.note: do is the emphatic polite request, as in do come in
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A polite request to work out, perhaps in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, which is what dousing means.

clue.text: V, when displayed in Europe, aces ignored

indicators.note: displayed in means shown within, so the answer sits among these words

explanation.surface: A rude V-sign shown in Europe when card players' aces are overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V' might be five or very; it is the two-finger gesture made palm outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-finger V gesture, palm out, is the symbol for peace.
